newsitem.title: CANADA: Shell Canada to sell chemicals business for $635 million.
newsitem.headline: Shell Canada to sell chemicals business for $635 million.

text.p: Shell Canada Ltd. said Tuesday it would sell its chemicals division to a unit of its corporate parent Royal Dutch/Shell Group for C$635 million ($467 million).
"We have made the decision to exit the chemical business," Shell Canada President Chuck Wilson said.

"While we have a world-scale, competitive styrene facility today, operating in a global chemical business based largely on one plant and one commodity chemical is in the long-run an unsustainable position," he said.

The deal, which would call for an affiliate of London-based Shell International Chemicals Ltd. to acquire a major Alberta styrene plant and isopropyl alcohol facilities in Ontario, was expected to be complete by the end of 1996, Shell Canada said.
Shell Canada, 78-percent owned by Royal Dutch/Shell, said it expected the sale to result in a C$200 million ($147 million) after-tax gain.
Under the arrangement, all current Shell Canada chemicals employees were expected to be retained by the new company, it said.

The sale includes Shell Canada's 450,000 metric ton per year styrene plant in Fort Saskatchewan, Alberta, and isoprpyl alcohol facilties in Sarnia, Ontario, as well as all related marketing activities.
